title: precheck says which part of a check fails, and planning checks pool rows with bench_pool's own predicates
goal: backlog.py precheck prints, for a failing check, its output, so a planner sees a check that fails for the wrong reason (SP-7y6dk257: ST-2p5ywkam's hand regex failed on one of six path-only rows and passed with four still path-only after the work); and the sprint planning rules ask a check over pool rows to call the code's own predicate (bench_pool.path_only, too_broad) rather than a new regex. Retrospective of SP-7y6dk257.
notes: SP-yzgetyu2 close (2026-10-09), accepted by the operator: ST-s6tqojsw's planned call-count check failed at plan on ModuleNotFoundError (runpy.run_path puts no _tools on sys.path), and precheck counted it as failing before the work, so the premise proved nothing and the check was fixed mid-run; a check that fails on an exception or traceback at plan is a broken check, not a failing premise, and precheck says so.
